Hosting family and friends can make your home a little busier during the holidays. With more meals being prepared, electronics being used, and people coming and going, your regular routine may look a bit different than usual.


As you prepare to welcome guests, a few minor changes can help you manage energy use while keeping everyone comfortable.


**Keep Your Home at a Comfortable Temperature**


More people at home can naturally add warmth indoors. Before adjusting the thermostat when guests arrive, give everyone some time to settle in and see how your home feels.


If everyone heads out for dinner, shopping, or another holiday activity, consider adjusting the thermostat while the house is empty. A programmable or smart thermostat can also help you maintain a comfortable temperature throughout the day.


**Make the Most of Holiday Cooking**


For many households, the kitchen is the gathering spot during the holidays. Planning ahead can help you make the most of the energy you’re already using.


When possible, cook multiple dishes at the same time if they require similar oven temperatures. Avoid opening the oven door more than necessary, as heat escapes each time it’s opened. For smaller dishes or leftovers, consider using a microwave, toaster oven, or other small appliance instead of heating the entire oven.


When it’s time to clean up, scrape off any remaining food and wait until the dishwasher is full before starting a load.


**Turn Off Electronics When They’re Not in Use**


TVs, gaming systems, speakers, and other electronics may get more use while everyone is home. When you’re finished using them, remember to turn them off.


If several devices are connected to the same entertainment system, a power strip can make it easier to turn them off at once. After guests leave, check for chargers or other devices that may still be plugged in.


**Be Mindful of Hot Water**


Overnight guests often means more hot water is used for showers, dishes, and laundry. To manage the additional energy needs that come with having a fuller house, wait until you have a full load before running the dishwasher or washing machine and use cold water for laundry when appropriate.


**Adjust the Lighting Around Your Home**


With guests moving between living spaces, it’s easy for lights to stay on in empty rooms. Remember to switch them off when a room is no longer being used.


For holiday lights and decorations, timers or smart plugs can help keep them on a regular schedule, so they don’t stay on longer than needed.


**Return to Your Normal Routine Once Guests Leave**


Once your guests travel home, take a few minutes to reset the spaces they used. Turn off lights or electronics that may have been left on and unplug any temporary devices.


If you adjusted your thermostat or smart home schedules while guests were visiting, remember to return them to their original settings.


**Enjoy the Holiday Season with Energy in Mind**


Having guests at home can change your routine, but managing energy doesn’t have to complicate your holiday plans. Making adjustments before, during, and after their stay can help keep your home comfortable while being energy conscious.
